cards.ex: Relate to means you understand something because you have felt or lived it too. Pattern: relate to someone or something. People often say I can totally relate, which means me too, I get it.
exs: Every tired mom in my chair can relate to my early mornings.
I can relate to that. I hate Mondays too.

cards.ex: At first sight means the very first time you see someone or something. The famous pattern is love at first sight. You can also say it looked easy at first sight, meaning at first glance.
exs: She loved the cat-eye style at first sight.
Do you believe in love at first sight?

cards.ex: Rush into means to start something too fast, without enough thinking. Pattern: rush into a relationship, a decision, or marriage. It's often used in advice: don't rush into it.
exs: Don't rush into a dramatic set. Try a natural one first.
They rushed into buying a house and regretted it.

cards.zh: 给…贴标签；给关系下定义
cards.ex: A label is a small tag with a name on it. As a verb, label means to give something a name or category. In dating, label the relationship means deciding if you're officially a couple.
exs: I label every glue bottle with the date I opened it.
We're dating, but we haven't put a label on it yet.

cards.ex: Attraction is the feeling of being pulled toward someone or something you like. Pattern: attraction to someone, physical attraction. A tourist attraction is a place people love to visit.
exs: The main attraction of lash extensions is waking up ready.
There was an instant attraction between them.

cards.ex: Intense means very strong, much stronger than usual. People say intense feelings, an intense workout, or he's a little intense, meaning too serious or too emotional. It's neutral and common.
exs: Some clients find a very dark lash look too intense.
That movie was so intense, I couldn't relax.

cards.ex: Steady means calm, stable, and not changing suddenly. People say a steady hand, a steady job, or a steady relationship. Going steady is an old phrase for dating one person.
exs: Lash work needs a really steady hand.
He has a steady job and a calm life.

cards.ex: Shared values are the important beliefs two people both have, like honesty, family, or hard work. People say we have shared values. It's often named as a key reason relationships last.
exs: My business partner and I have shared values about honest pricing.
Shared values matter more than shared hobbies.

cards.ex: A flaw is a small weakness or mistake in someone or something. People say everyone has flaws, or a flaw in the plan. It's a little more formal than a bad point.
exs: I check every set for flaws before the client opens her eyes.
He accepts my flaws, and I accept his.

cards.ex: Impress means to make someone admire you. Pattern: impress someone, try to impress someone, be impressed by something. On a first date, people often try too hard to impress.
exs: I wanted to impress my first client, so I took my time.
She cooked a huge dinner to impress his parents.

cards.ex: A spark is a tiny flash of fire. In love, it means a sudden exciting feeling between two people. People say there was no spark, or the spark is gone.
exs: That first lash class lit a spark in me.
We had fun, but there was no spark.

cards.ex: The honeymoon phase is the early, perfect-feeling time in a relationship or new job, when everything seems wonderful. People say we're still in the honeymoon phase. It usually doesn't last forever.
exs: I'm still in the honeymoon phase with my new studio.
The honeymoon phase ended when we started living together.

cards.zh: 吃过苦头才明白；吃一堑长一智
cards.ex: Learn something the hard way means you learn a lesson through a bad experience, not from advice. Pattern: I learned it the hard way, or learn the hard way that something is true.
exs: I learned the hard way to always do a patch test.
He learned the hard way not to text while driving.

cards.ex: Warning signs are small clues that something bad might happen. People say ignore the warning signs, or watch for warning signs. A casual version is red flags.
exs: Red, itchy eyes are warning signs of an allergy.
I ignored the warning signs in that relationship.

cards.ex: Fade means to slowly become weaker, lighter, or quieter until it almost disappears. People say the color faded, the feeling faded, or fade away. It's about slow change, not sudden change.
exs: Lash tint usually fades after a few weeks.
The excitement faded, but the love stayed.

cards.ex: Awkward means uncomfortable or embarrassing, especially in social situations. People say an awkward silence, an awkward moment, or this is awkward. It's very common in casual speech.
exs: It's awkward when a client falls asleep and snores.
There was an awkward silence after his joke.

cards.ex: Grounded means calm, stable, and connected to real life, like your feet are firmly on the ground. People say she's very grounded, or I feel grounded. Grounded can also mean a teen can't go out.
exs: Morning walks keep me grounded before a busy day.
He's very grounded. Nothing makes him panic.

cards.ex: Mature means acting like a thoughtful adult, calm and responsible. People say a mature decision, or she's mature for her age. The opposite is immature, which is childish.
exs: Handling that angry client so calmly was very mature.
It was a mature way to end the relationship.

cards.ex: Anxiety is a feeling of worry and nervousness, often about the future. The adjective is anxious. People say anxiety about something, or social anxiety. It's more serious than just being a little worried.
exs: Some clients have anxiety about lying still with their eyes closed.
Waiting for the results gave me so much anxiety.

cards.ex: Overthink means to think about something too much, until it becomes stressful. People say I'm overthinking it, or stop overthinking. The noun is overthinking. It's casual and very common.
exs: I overthink every message from a new client.
Don't overthink it. Just text him back.

cards.ex: Drama is a type of play or show, but in daily life it means emotional conflict and fighting. People say I don't want any drama, or she loves drama. The adjective is dramatic.
exs: I keep my salon drama-free.
Their relationship has way too much drama.

cards.ex: Dull means boring, with nothing interesting or exciting. It can also mean not bright or not sharp, like a dull color or a dull knife. Boring is the more casual word.
exs: Dull tweezers make lash work so much harder.
The meeting was long and dull.

cards.zh: （心动或紧张时）心里小鹿乱撞
cards.ex: Butterflies, or butterflies in your stomach, is a nervous, excited feeling, like small wings moving inside you. People say I get butterflies before a date or a big event.
exs: I still get butterflies before a bridal appointment.
He gave me butterflies the first time we talked.

cards.ex: A foundation is the strong base under a building. People also use it for relationships and skills: a strong foundation, or build a foundation. Foundation is also a type of makeup.
exs: Good lash mapping is the foundation of every great set.
Trust is the foundation of any relationship.

cards.ex: Underestimate means to think something is smaller, easier, or less important than it really is. Pattern: underestimate someone or something. Don't underestimate means take it seriously. The opposite is overestimate.
exs: I underestimated how long a mega volume set takes.
Never underestimate the power of a good night's sleep.

cards.ex: Swipe means to move your finger quickly across a screen. On dating apps, swipe right means yes, and swipe left means no. You also swipe a card to pay.
exs: Clients swipe through my photos to choose a style.
She swiped left on every guy in a suit.

cards.ex: Move on means to stop thinking about something in the past and continue with your life. Pattern: move on from something. People use it after breakups, mistakes, or bad days.
exs: One bad review hurt, but I moved on.
It took her a year to move on from the breakup.

cards.zh: 脆弱的；（主动）敞开内心的
cards.ex: Vulnerable means easy to hurt. In relationships, being vulnerable means showing your true feelings and fears, which takes courage. The noun is vulnerability. People say feel vulnerable, or be vulnerable with someone.
exs: Clients feel a little vulnerable with their eyes closed, so I talk them through it.
It's hard for him to be vulnerable.

cards.ex: Open up means to start sharing your real thoughts and feelings with someone. Pattern: open up to someone, or open up about something. It's casual and very common.
exs: Clients often open up to me about their lives during a long set.
She finally opened up about her past.

cards.ex: In disguise means hidden under a different look. The common phrase is a blessing in disguise, which means something that seemed bad but turned out good.
exs: Losing that job was a blessing in disguise. It pushed me to open my studio.
He came to the party in disguise.

cards.ex: Take over means to take control of something, or to fill all the space. Pattern: take over something, or let something take over your life. It's casual and common.
exs: I won't let work take over my weekends.
Her new hobby has taken over her whole apartment.

cards.ex: Make it official means to formally announce or confirm something, especially that two people are a couple. People ask, when will you make it official? It's casual.
exs: I finally made it official and registered my business.
They made it official on Instagram.

cards.ex: Sustainable means something can continue for a long time without breaking down. People say a sustainable lifestyle, sustainable fashion, or a sustainable pace. It sounds slightly formal.
exs: Seeing eight clients a day isn't sustainable for me.
A healthy diet has to be sustainable, not extreme.

cards.ex: Compromise means both people give up a little so they can agree. People say we need to compromise, or reach a compromise. It's a key word for healthy relationships and work.
exs: The client wanted longer lashes, so we compromised on a medium length.
We compromised: I pick dinner, he picks the movie.

cards.ex: Compatibility means two people or things work well together. The adjective is compatible. People say we're compatible, or compatibility matters more than chemistry. It also works for phones and apps.
exs: Glue and humidity compatibility really matters in summer.
They have great compatibility, even with different hobbies.

cards.ex: Wrap up means to finish something, like wrapping a gift at the end. People say let's wrap up, or wrap up a meeting. It's casual and friendly, perfect for ending conversations.
exs: I wrap up every appointment with aftercare tips.
Let's wrap up and get some dinner.

cards.ex: Trust your instincts means to follow your natural feeling about what's right, without overthinking. People also say trust your gut. It's common advice for big decisions.
exs: I trust my instincts when a style won't suit someone's eyes.
If the deal feels wrong, trust your instincts.
